intro: A button drops off a coat on the coldest morning of the year. A backpack seam opens and books slide out onto the bus floor. A great jacket at the thrift store is one inch too long in the sleeves. Every one of those problems can be fixed in under an hour with a needle, a spool of thread and a set of skills that people carried in their hands for thousands of years before anyone had a sewing machine. This unit teaches those skills from the first knot.

The first chapter is the kit and the seven stitches. You will learn what every tool in a sewing kit does, how to choose a needle and thread, how to thread the eye and roll a knot that holds, and how to handle pins and needles so nobody gets hurt. Then you will sew seven stitches on a practice square: running, basting, back, whip, slip, blanket and overcast. Each one has a job, and by the end you will know which to reach for and why.

The second chapter puts the stitches to work. You will sew a button with a shank, attach a hook and eye and a snap, measure and hem a pair of pants so nothing shows, mend a split seam, patch a hole, and read a simple pattern to make a drawstring pouch from start to finish. You will finish by putting numbers on the choice to mend or replace, and by looking at where clothes go when nobody mends them. By the end, a torn seam will be ten minutes of your time, not a reason to throw something away.
bigQuestion: What can one needle and one thread do that keeps clothes, and the people who wear them, in good shape?

timeline.t: People shape the earliest known eyed needles from bone and ivory to sew hides together
Egyptians spin flax into linen thread and sew garments with copper and bone needles
Redditch, England grows into the center of steel needle making, turning needles into a cheap everyday tool
Patrick Clark of Paisley, Scotland begins spinning cotton sewing thread as a substitute for silk
Barthélemy Thimonnier builds an early chain-stitch sewing machine in France
Elias Howe patents a lockstitch sewing machine in the United States
Walter Hunt patents the safety pin, a bent wire with a guarded point
Isaac Singer's machine puts sewing machines into homes and factories across America
Whitcomb Judson shows a clasp fastener at the Chicago World's Fair, an ancestor of the zipper
The Smith-Hughes Act funds home economics in U.S. schools, and sewing becomes a classroom subject
Polyester thread and fabric arrive, strong and cheap, and clothing prices begin a long fall
U.S. EPA reports about 17 million tons of textile waste in a year, most of it landfilled

words.d: a small cap worn on the middle finger to push the needle through fabric
all-purpose hand needles with a round eye and a sharp point; a higher number means a finer needle
a simple in-and-out stitch that looks like a dashed line, used for gathering and light seams
long, loose temporary stitches in contrasting thread that hold fabric until the real seam is sewn
a stitch that returns to the end of the last stitch, making the strongest hand seam
a stitch that wraps over the edge of two layers to join them quickly
a nearly invisible stitch that travels inside a fold and catches one or two threads of the outer fabric
an edge stitch that makes upright stitches joined by a line of thread along the edge
slanted stitches wrapped over a raw edge to stop woven fabric from fraying
how tightly the thread is pulled; too tight puckers, too loose loops
a short stem of thread under a button that leaves room for the buttonhole layer
the fabric folded up inside a hem, usually 1 1/2 to 2 inches on pants

test.q: Which tool is worn on the finger to push a needle through thick fabric?
test.why: The thimble caps the middle finger so the needle is pushed with metal, not skin.

test.q: A size 9 sharp compared to a size 5 sharp is:
test.why: With hand needles, a higher number means a finer, shorter needle.

test.q: About how long should you cut a piece of thread for hand sewing?
test.why: Around 18 inches is long enough for a seam and short enough not to tangle.

test.q: A knot keeps pulling through loosely woven fabric. What should you do?
choices: Tie a second knot on top of the first
test.why: A bigger knot cannot pass through the weave. A second knot on the first solves it.

test.q: Which stitch looks like a dashed line and is used to gather fabric?
test.why: The in-and-out running stitch leaves dashes and can be pulled to gather fabric into folds.

test.q: Why does a back stitch hold better than a running stitch?
choices: Each stitch overlaps and locks the one before it
It is sewn on the outside
test.why: The overlapping thread locks every stitch, so the seam does not slide or unravel.

choices: Tight, short and in matching thread
Long, loose and in a contrasting color
test.why: Basting is temporary, so it should be easy to see, easy to remove and out of the way of the real seam.

test.q: Which stitch would you use to hem dress pants so the stitches do not show?
test.why: The slip stitch hides in the fold and catches one or two threads, so only tiny dots show.

test.q: Fleece does not need an overcast edge because:
choices: It is too thick to sew
test.why: Overcasting stops fraying. Fleece, felt and knits do not fray, so they do not need it.

test.q: Fabric puckers into ridges along a seam. The cause is:
choices: A needle that is too fine
test.why: Ridges mean tension that is too tight. Pull only until the thread lies flat.

test.q: When an iron is not in your hand, it should be:
test.why: On its heel, the hot plate is off the board and away from fabric and hands.

test.q: What is the purpose of winding thread under a button after sewing through the holes?
choices: To make a shank that leaves room for the buttonhole layer
To keep the toothpick in place
test.why: The wraps build a thread shank, so the other fabric layer fits under the button without bunching.

test.q: To mend a split seam, you should sew:
choices: Only across the gap, stopping at each end
On the outside with a whip stitch
A back stitch along the old line, about 1/2 inch past each end of the split
A running stitch in bright thread
test.why: Overlapping the sound stitches on both ends locks the mend so the seam cannot reopen at its edges.

test.q: A patch on a worn knee should be stitched:
choices: Into the thin fabric next to the hole
With single thread and long stitches
All the way around, onto sound fabric beyond the worn area
test.why: Stitches must land on fabric that can hold them, and the patch must be fastened on all sides.

test.q: According to EPA figures for 2018, roughly what share of U.S. textile waste was landfilled?
test.why: About 11.3 of 17 million tons went to landfills, close to two thirds.

write.prompt: A friend hands you a pair of pants with a split side seam, a missing button on the back pocket and cuffs that are two inches too long. Write the steps you would take to fix all three, in order, naming the stitch and the tools for each job, and explain why each step is there.
tips: Put the three jobs in a sensible order and say why that order.
Name the stitch for each job and the reason it is the right one.
Include the safety rules for pins, needles and the iron.
Give the real numbers: thread length, stitch size, hem allowance, how many wraps for the shank.
End with how you would check each repair before handing the pants back.
